_meta.method: Side-by-side synthesis of every key US-vs-China metric tracked on this site, plus the SemiAnalysis Unitree and robotics-supply-chain analyses. The 'Traditional arms vs cobots' section (added 2026-06-18) draws on FAI's 'The State of Industrial Robotics' (Michael & Alden, 2026).

bluf.headline: China leads where robots are bought, built, and priced; the U.S. leads where they think and who funds them.
bluf.body: China buys 54% of the world's industrial robots, hosts >80% of humanoid installations, controls ~70% of the parts chain, and ships humanoids at one-third the U.S. build cost. The U.S. counters with the robot brains (NVIDIA compute, foundation models), the deepest capital markets ($23B+ VC in 2026 YTD, Figure at $39B), and a rebuilding effort at both ends of the supply chain. The contested middle — components, batteries, sensors — decides who wins the decade.

sections.title: Traditional arms vs cobots — the AI leading indicator

metrics.us: Not a producer — no US firm makes heavy-duty arms; Adept was sold to Omron, Rethink's assets to Germany's HAHN. Relies on Japanese & European imports
metrics.china: Secondary player — passed Japan in unit production share in 2024, but no Chinese firm tops 2% of the global arm market and median Chinese-firm margins run under 1% vs over 4% industry-wide
metrics.note: Neither superpower leads here: Japan + Europe (FANUC, Yaskawa, ABB, KUKA) hold ~85% of arm revenue. Between the US and China, only China produces at volume.

metrics.us: A few small entrants (Standard Bots); negligible global share
metrics.china: Over half of global cobot shipments since 2023; after Denmark's Universal Robots (~30%), most of the top cobot makers are Chinese

metrics.us: Imports the bulk of its cobots
metrics.china: ~90% of domestic cobot demand met by Chinese makers — versus ~60% for industrial robots overall

metrics.us: Leads the AI layer — foundation models and compute — but not the cheap, AI-integrated hardware that will carry it
metrics.china: Cobots are only ~12% of installs but proxy the AI-integrated future: cheaper, software-heavy, easy to deploy. China's cobot lead signals its likely position as arms go AI-native
metrics.note: Incumbents' high-precision, heavy-payload dominance matters less as inexpensive AI-integrated systems spread.

unitree_case.title: Case study: Unitree vs the U.S. humanoid stack
unitree_case.intro: SemiAnalysis calls Unitree the proof of the 'DJI strategy' — bootstrap through researchers and hobbyists, own the bottleneck components, then ride ecosystem maturity into every adjacent market. Here is how it stacks against the American approach, dimension by dimension.

rows.us_oems: Figure 350+ built; Agility single-digit volumes; Optimus not shipped externally

rows.unitree: $50K+ → $27.3K in 12–18 months; under $20K in some deals; G1 from ~$16K
rows.us_oems: No public price; BOM alone ~$46K with Chinese parts, $131K without

rows.unitree: ~67% on the G1 — profitable while cutting prices
rows.us_oems: Pre-commercial; burn funded by venture capital

rows.unitree: Self-developed BLDC motors (30–40% of Western motor cost), planetary gearboxes, lidars, depth cameras
rows.us_oems: Figure builds actuators/packs in-house at BotQ; Tesla designs in-house but buys volume parts from Sanhua/Tuopu (China)

rows.unitree: G1 entirely decoupled from American components
rows.us_oems: No US humanoid is decoupled from China — magnets, reducers, screws all flow through Chinese chokepoints

rows.unitree: The leading platform for humanoid AI research — NVIDIA's open GR00T reference humanoid is built on a Unitree H2 Plus chassis
rows.us_oems: US labs buy Unitrees to train American foundation models on Chinese hardware

rows.unitree: Buys US chip designs; frontier autonomy models are not Chinese
rows.us_oems: NVIDIA compute, foundation models (Helix, π0, GR00T), capital depth, and Amazon-scale deployment demand
